name: PRF / PRP face contouring

lead: PRP and PRF are made by spinning a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and growth factors, then injecting or applying them to the face.
They are marketed for skin rejuvenation; evidence overall is described as mixed.

paras: Platelets release growth factors thought to stimulate tissue repair [1].
Adverse effects are generally low, though improper equipment reuse caused a 2024 HIV cluster at an unlicensed spa [1].

lead: PRF and PRP face contouring refers to using platelet-rich plasma or platelet-rich fibrin, concentrates made from a patient's own blood, to add volume or improve the skin of the face.

Platelet-rich plasma is a blood fraction with platelet levels typically 3 to 5 times normal, believed to release growth factors that aid healing [1]. Aesthetic clinics use it for wrinkles and fine lines, often with microneedling in "vampire facials" [1]. Wikipedia describes the evidence overall as mixed [1].
Registered trials of platelet-rich fibrin focus on dental and nerve applications; a small trial of PRF in a face cream is the nearest to cosmetic use [2].
infobox: PRP itself exempt; preparation devices require clearance

paras: PRP is spun in a centrifuge to remove red cells while keeping platelets; preparation varies between clinics and kits, so the product differs by location [1].

Adverse effects are low in most trials [1]. In 2024 the CDC reported three HIV diagnoses among patients of an unlicensed New Mexico spa that reused contaminated single-use equipment, an infection-control failure [1].

Registered studies include PRF in a face care cream for skin ageing (phase 2, n=20) [2], PRF in third molar surgery for swelling [3], PRF with nerve repair after facial nerve injury (n=21) [4] and injectable PRF for gum thickness and esthetic-zone sockets [5][6]. None tests PRF or PRP as a facial volume or contouring treatment.

timeline.event: Interest in PRP for hair loss begins [1].
